items.headline: Fed holds rates at 3.75%-4.00% in 10-2 split vote; two governors dissent for a hike
items.summary: The FOMC kept the fed funds rate unchanged, with Gov. Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed's Beth Hammack dissenting in favor of a 25bp hike. The statement upgraded growth language to "expanding at a strong pace" while calling inflation "elevated," and December hike odds on CME FedWatch rose to 82.6% from 78.3%.
items.actionable: A hawkish hold with rising December hike odds is a near-term headwind for non-yielding gold/silver positions -- watch for real-yield pressure on SLV/GDX into the next data prints.

items.headline: Microsoft beats on Q1 FY27 earnings; Alphabet drops on miss and negative cash flow
items.summary: Microsoft reported revenue of $92.3B (+19% YoY) and non-GAAP EPS of $4.89 vs. $4.73 consensus, with Azure cloud revenue up 48% as guided; shares rose ~4-5% after-hours. Alphabet missed on EPS ($2.12 vs $3.02 expected) partly on an $8.2B unrealized SpaceX markdown and swung to negative free cash flow, even as Google Cloud revenue grew 103%; shares fell ~10-11% after-hours.
items.actionable: Confirms the AI-capex supercycle is still intact (bullish megacap tech, risk-on tone) but Alphabet's cash-flow strain and Google's ad-growth deceleration are a read-through risk for Tencent's own AI-capex ramp and negative-FCF trend.

items.headline: Gold slips to ~$4,049-4,055/oz, silver falls to ~$53.91 ahead of Fed; gold-silver ratio hits 75.1
items.summary: Gold spot eased about 0.28% and silver fell roughly 0.94% on the day ahead of the FOMC decision. The gold-silver ratio climbed to 75.1, up from ~60 at the start of the year, as silver slides toward its yearly low against a firmer gold floor.
items.actionable: Silver's underperformance is widening the gold/silver ratio toward multi-year extremes -- a potential mean-reversion setup for SLV/SILJ/AG if the ratio rolls over, but near-term momentum still favors gold over silver.

items.headline: Mothballed silver mills and historic mine sites being reactivated as supply crunch persists
items.summary: Industry reporting highlights miners bringing idled mills and historic sites back into production plans as the 2025-26 physical silver shortage persists. This follows a period where London lease rates spiked above 30-39% in October before moderating to roughly 11%, still far above the sub-1% historical norm.
items.actionable: Supply-side response (restarting mothballed capacity) confirms the structural silver deficit is being taken seriously by producers -- supportive for mine-life extension and project-expansion narratives at AG/HL/PAAS.

items.headline: Brent tops $114.87, WTI $101.49 as Houthis strike Saudi targets and US weighs renewed Iran campaign
items.summary: Saudi coalition forces intercepted a Houthi ballistic missile aimed at Taif and the Houthis claimed a drone strike on Abha airport. The WSJ reported Washington has warned Gulf states to prepare for a possible renewed US military campaign against Iran after the Nov 3 US midterms, even as Qatari mediators present Tehran a new draft deal.
items.actionable: Elevated Hormuz/Houthi risk keeps an inflation and tail-risk bid under gold/silver even as the Fed stays hawkish -- a geopolitical offset worth tracking against the rate-driven headwind.

items.headline: China confirms US-China trade truce extended to Jan 10, 2027, but rare-earth-specific confirmation still pending
items.summary: China's Ministry of Commerce confirmed on Sept 28 that trade arrangements with the US are extended to Jan 10, 2027, following Treasury Secretary Bessent's Sept 23 announcement of the same date -- pushing back the widely-feared Nov 10 expiry. However, the MOFCOM statement did not explicitly name rare earths, so formal confirmation that the rare-earth export-control suspension itself is extended is still awaited as of late October.
items.actionable: The broader trade truce extension to Jan 2027 reduces (but does not eliminate) Nov 10 cliff-edge risk for rare-earth supply chains -- stay alert for Beijing's explicit rare-earth-specific notice, which remains the real trigger for the group.

items.headline: Rare earth equities ease again: USAR -3%, MP eases, Critical Metals -7% amid ongoing US-China uncertainty
items.summary: USA Rare Earth fell about 3% to $10.07 and MP Materials eased on Oct 28 as the sector continues to digest shifting US-China trade signals; Critical Metals dropped 7% on a dilutive European lithium deal. MP will report Q3 earnings Nov 5, having flagged higher NdPr output, a Texas magnet campus, and a JV with Saudi's Maaden and the Department of War for a Saudi refinery.
items.actionable: Near-term rare-earth equity weakness looks like a "buy the execution, not the narrative" setup -- MP's Nov 5 print (first post-shipping quarter) is the next real catalyst for the watchlist rather than more deadline headlines.

items.headline: Lynas signs binding deal to acquire Meteoric Resources for ~A$968m; stock still down 42% in 6 months
items.summary: On Oct 1, Lynas signed a binding scheme implementation deed to acquire Meteoric Resources (owner of the Caldeira ionic-clay rare-earth deposit in Brazil) for about A$968m in stock, even as Lynas's share price has fallen 42% over six months despite a record FY26 profit (+76% revenue, +282% EBITDA).
items.actionable: Lynas is using weak share-price currency to buy growth (Brazil ionic-clay feedstock) rather than returning cash -- diversification positive long-term but near-term dilution/integration risk for LYC.AX holders.

items.headline: PLA sustains gray-zone pressure on Taiwan Strait; 169 aircraft, 321 vessels tracked since Oct 1
items.summary: Taiwan's MND reports continuous near-daily PLA aircraft/vessel incursions, including a live-fire drill on Oct 14 using four Type 071 amphibious landing ships and harassment of Taiwanese vessels by 12 China Coast Guard/research ships on Oct 18. No escalation beyond established gray-zone patterns has been reported this week.
items.actionable: Taiwan Strait tension remains elevated but non-escalatory -- a persistent background risk premium on HK/China tech rather than an acute trigger; no change to position sizing warranted on this alone.

items.headline: Tencent-JD forge AI agent e-commerce alliance; Tencent leases AI chips from Oracle as capex weighs on FCF
items.summary: Tencent and JD.com announced an AI-agent partnership targeting e-commerce fulfillment, while Tencent separately agreed to lease AI chips from Oracle (~$7B over 5 years) as its own AI capex (RMB52.8bn in Q2) pushed free cash flow negative. JD and Xiaomi are both ramping Nov 11 ("Double 11") shopping-festival promotions, with JD citing ~3 million foldable-phone preorders.
items.actionable: Tencent's capex-driven negative FCF is a near-term earnings-quality concern worth monitoring into its next print, while Double 11 prep is a modest tactical positive for JD/Xiaomi consumer volumes this quarter.

items.headline: Keppel REIT falls 4.85% on SGD626.2m sponsor acquisition; CapitaLand China Trust Q3 NPI/revenue down 5.1%
items.summary: Keppel REIT units dropped to SGD0.785 (-4.85%) on Oct 20 after announcing a SGD626.2m acquisition from its sponsor, raising dilution/funding concerns. Separately, CapitaLand China Trust posted a 5.1% YoY decline in property income for Q3/9M2026 and was downgraded to HOLD with fair value cut to SGD0.615 from SGD0.665.
items.actionable: Both Keppel REIT (acquisition/dilution risk) and CapitaLand China Trust (China retail/office softness) are showing idiosyncratic weakness independent of the broader SG REIT sector -- reassess sizing ahead of any further distribution guidance.

items.headline: DBS to report Nov 5, OCBC Nov 6; October bank selloff judged not a fundamental breakdown
items.summary: DBS reports Q3 on Nov 5 and OCBC on Nov 6 (UOB expected second week of November). Commentary notes the October SG bank selloff isn't a sign of fundamental breakdown given solid H1 2026 results: DBS earned S$6.01B H1 net profit (ROE 17.5%), OCBC's H1 net profit rose 13% to a record S$4.2B.
items.actionable: Fundamentals look intact into the Nov 5-6 prints; the October selloff looks more like a rate/sentiment de-rating than credit deterioration, supporting a hold-through-earnings stance on DBS/OCBC.

items.headline: Bitcoin holds above $81,000; spot ETFs post second straight day of inflows but Glassnode flags $78K downside test
items.summary: Bitcoin traded near $81,000-81,400, with US spot Bitcoin ETFs pulling in $176M on Tuesday (second consecutive inflow day), narrowing October's net ETF outflows to just $26M after sharp mid-month withdrawals. Glassnode's latest note (Oct 29) warns BTC could retest $78K as ETF buying support fades.
items.actionable: ETF flows have stabilized but remain fragile post-Fed; the $78K Glassnode downside level is the near-term risk marker for crypto-correlated sentiment spillover into risk assets broadly.
